name: Seletinoid G

lead: Seletinoid G is an experimental retinoid designed with computer modelling by Korean researchers to treat aged skin with less irritation than tretinoin. The payoff sought is fewer wrinkles and smoother skin from retinoid-style renewal at a gentler level.

As a retinoid it is meant to act on skin cells to influence extracellular matrix proteins such as collagen. Human data are a 2005 experiment in 23 volunteers using occlusive application on the buttocks for four days, plus 2020 skin-model work on barrier function and wound healing. No patient trials are known.

paras: It is not a marketed approved drug, so there is no standard routine. It appears in research on topical anti-aging and skin-barrier repair.
Its stated aim was lower irritation than tretinoin, based on the small 2005 comparison. It has no approved status and no long-term safety data were found.

angle.text: Seletinoid G is a lab-designed retinoid intended to renew aged and photoaged skin with less irritation than tretinoin, aiming for fewer wrinkles and smoother skin. Human data come from a 23-person, four-day study plus skin-model work.

lead: Seletinoid G is an experimental synthetic retinoid that was designed with computer-aided molecular modeling by Korean researchers as a topical anti-aging ingredient intended to cause less skin irritation than all-trans retinoic acid (tretinoin).[1] Published work on it concerns aged and photoaged skin, with a related line of laboratory work on skin barrier repair.[1][2]

The published human evidence is limited to a small short-term in vivo experiment in 23 volunteers using occlusive application on the buttocks, reported in 2005, and to laboratory work in reconstructed human skin models in 2020.[1][2] No large randomized trials of seletinoid G for wrinkles or acne have been identified, and it is not an approved drug. Discussion of it in looksmaxxing communities was not found in the available sources.

paras: Seletinoid G has been investigated as a cosmetic-type active for aged skin. The stated rationale in its 2005 report was that retinoids have potential efficacy in aged skin but that skin irritation limits their use, and that a newly designed molecule might retain activity with less irritation.[1]

A 2005 study tested seletinoid G against all-trans retinoic acid in 23 subjects, applying each for four days under occlusion on the buttocks, and assessed skin irritation and the expression of extracellular matrix proteins in the skin.[1] It is a short mechanistic experiment rather than a trial of visible wrinkle improvement on the face.

Later work, published in 2020, used human skin equivalents (laboratory-grown skin models) rather than patients, and examined epidermal barrier function, wound healing and collagen realignment.[2] No randomized controlled trials in patients are listed in the sources reviewed.

Laboratory work has examined its effects on keratinocyte-mediated wound closure and collagen organization in skin models, framed by the authors as relevant to anti-aging because wound healing is impaired in older skin.[2] A separate 2019 paper from the same institute concerns kojyl cinnamate ester derivatives and hair growth factors in dermal papilla cells; it is a different compound class and is not evidence about seletinoid G itself.[3]

timeline.event: Seletinoid G reported as a computer-designed retinoid and tested in 23 volunteers against tretinoin.[1]
Study in human skin equivalents examines barrier function, wound healing and collagen realignment.[2]
